keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for an association, never coloured as territory (rule 4). The page: infobox area '1801: 34,314 km2' and 'As of 1792 the Swabian Circle consisted of 88 territories'; Austrian Swabia was not a member ('did not include the Habsburg home territories of Swabian Austria'). The stand-in is the gazetteer's Baden-Wurttemberg plus a 40 km circle at Augsburg (Bavarian Swabia), less the gazetteer's Franconia region: about 39,700 km2 in gazetteer cells, 1.16 times the page figure. The member list on the page is selected; the Allgau, Hohenzollern and Lake Constance members are inside the stand-in only roughly.

ledger.note: 1500: the Swabian Circle was 'established in 1500 on the territory of the former German stem-duchy of Swabia' (infobox 'Established: 1500'). The page does not date the Reichstag of Augsburg that created the circles. Review follow-up: the counterpart was holy-roman-empire, whose dossier ends in 1259; changed to holy-roman-empire-minor-states (Cliopatria's 1260..1806 row).

1803: the directors change. 'The directors of the Swabian Circle were the' Bishop of Constance and the Duke of Württemberg; the Bishop was replaced by the margrave of Baden 'after the 1803 Reichsdeputationshauptschluss', which reduced the number of members from 88 (1792) to 41.

1806: the circle ends. 'The Reichsdeputationshauptschluss reduced the number to 41 and the 1806 Rheinbundakte to seven' (infobox 'Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire: 1806'; the infobox also gives 'Disestablished: 1808'). Review follow-up: the counterpart was holy-roman-empire, whose dossier ends in 1259; changed to holy-roman-empire-minor-states (Cliopatria's 1260..1806 row).

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New association (type umbrella): Cliopatria has no row for the Imperial Circles, and the brief names the Swabian and Franconian Circles. Rule 4: an association of estates is never territory; the shape below is a coarse reading of its member lands for the reviewer, not for colouring. The member territories with their own dossiers (Wurttemberg, Baden, Konstanz, Augsburg ...) carry the land.

SHAPE. Gazetteer Baden-Wurttemberg plus a 40 km circle at Augsburg, minus the gazetteer's Franconia region: about 39,700 km2 against the page's 34,314 km2 (1801). Gazetteer names wanted: none new (Augsburg, Baden-Wurttemberg and Franconia resolve).

DATES. 1500 (page; infobox 'Established: 1500'), 1803 (Bishop of Constance replaced by Baden as director) and 1806 (Rheinbundakte, 'to seven' members; infobox 'Disestablished: 1808' is not used). The page dates the army at Kehl ('from 1694 on even maintained its own army based at the Kehl fortress') but no war of the circle; no war entry.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The page's member list is selected, and the 88 territories of 1792 are not listed; (2) no creation month or Reichstag; (3) the infobox end (1808) against the text (1806).

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new.

The reviewer failed this dossier because its type is umbrella: an Imperial Circle is an association of estates, never territory (brief rule 4), and its shape overlays the member states that have dossiers of their own. That is an orchestrator decision (drop the file, or keep it only if the compiler skips type umbrella); the brief for this batch asked for the circle and rule 4 says 'type: umbrella for associations', so the file is left in place and its type unchanged. The only change made: the found and dissolve counterpart holy-roman-empire (dossier ends 1259) is now holy-roman-empire-minor-states.
